worker_notes: Identity independently checked in the supplied canonical text: title Gay Asian Americans Are Seen as More American Than Asian Americans Who Are Presumed Straight; authors Mika Semrow, Linda X. Zou, Shuyang Liu, and Sapna Cheryan; DOI 10.1177/1948550619849426; original journal research article, Social Psychological and Personality Science 2020, 11(3), 336–344, copyright 2019. The candidate is a full paginated article parse, including methods, results, discussion, and references, rather than an abstract or secondary report. No PDF path was supplied; layout rendering was unavailable within the authorized sources. Study 4 reports 101 recruited students across recruitment channels (44 subject-pool, 57 campus), but does not explicitly identify the final participant count for the critical mixed-model ANOVA or explain analytic exclusions. The ANOVA reports denominator df 98; N must not be inferred from df. The manipulation-check denominators 100 and 99 are not explicitly documented mutually exclusive final participant groups and must not be summed. Thus analytic N cannot be established under the assigned evidence rule. Target correspondence follows the named Study 4 factors and outcome, not row order or numerical agreement. Only assigned unfinished fields were completed; all other value fields are placeholders. The acceptance main effect is explicitly distinguished from the sexual-orientation interaction and the gay-target simple effect. Retained printed dav .34 without conversion to between-groups d. Same-test p is printed as p ¼ .005; p is unassigned and remains a placeholder.
